claims.text: All three artifacts describe the same trip — trip_id TRP-00111 and the 07:47:40 start appear on the trip record, the trace and the fare ledger — so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; and on the governing distance the trip ran 29.98 km against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km or 24.92%, which passes both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20%). The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence and the rider has discharged her initial burden.

The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 29.98 km, not the trip record's rounded 30.0 km; the trace figure is the one POL-RD-01 makes the threshold test run on, and it is the trace's 229 fixes at 10 second intervals with 100% coverage and no gaps that carry the excess of 5.98 km. The rider asks that the establishment test be run on that field and not on the convenience copy.

The fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route: no upfront quote was fixed at booking, and POL-RD-02 is therefore the operative remedy on this trip rather than a pass-through-only correction.

No exculpatory route other than the closure is open to the driver: the booked optimum of 24.0 km stands because the trip record carries no pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no re-quote exists; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not substitute a matched-itinerary baseline and solo_optimal_distance_km is irrelevant here.

The chat log records no instruction from the rider. Her only message, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver: with waypoint_hint null and no road named the corroboration test cannot be run at all, and a reply fixing a time of arrival cannot be converted into a rider-requested detour that would exonerate the excess.

The driver's only route to exculpation is POL-RD-03, and that exoneration is capped: the justified excess is the lesser of the measured excess and 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00, computed from the advisory's own shortest_lawful_alternative_km on the record, and any distance beyond that cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal. The rider asks the judge to run that cap on this record's figures rather than treating the existence of the advisory as excusing the whole of the trip, and to refund whatever the cap does not cover.

On the rider's primary case, that the closure does not account for the whole of the excess, POL-RD-02 requires the ruling to state charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund on separate lines: recomputed on the booked optimum, ((3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 31.00 against a charged_total of 37.74, an overcharge of 6.74; the payable figure is then rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor applies.

The rider's profile does not engage the extra corroboration rule in POL-RD-08: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4 that the clause sets (and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, which only matters once the count reaches 4), so her claim of 24.92% excess is subject to the ordinary burden and needs no corroboration beyond the trace.

claims.text: The booked optimal route runs BKE southbound then PIE westbound, and the LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 closes the PIE towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit, between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit, from 07:10 to 09:30 on the morning of the trip. That is the exact expressway segment the optimal route traverses, it is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE, its geometry intersects the route (intersects_route true) and its validity window brackets the entire trip (overlaps_trip_window true). The first limb of POL-RD-03 is therefore satisfied on the face of the advisory, not on the driver's say-so.

The second and third limbs of POL-RD-03 are met too. The advisory directs a diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd, and the driver's route was Upper Bukit Timah then the AYE - the route leaves the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoins it further on. The trace is clean corroboration of a deliberate diversion rather than a wander: 229 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, with speeds varying by road class (0.0 / 20.6 / 46.5 / 71.0 kph) as an expressway-then-arterial-then-expressway route would. The advisory's shortest_lawful_alternative_km of 29.2 km sits almost exactly on the trace's 29.98 km.

The exoneration cap in POL-RD-03 is not reached, so the whole excess is excused. The cap is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The justified excess is therefore the entire measured excess, the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, and no excess survives for POL-RD-02 to refund. Note the governing distance figure is the trace's 29.98 km, not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record, as POL-RD-01 requires.

Even if the tribunal declined to exonerate in full, the arithmetic still lands on NO_ACTION. Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route - 29.98 km at a duration of 30.0 x (29.98 / 24.0) = 37.5 minutes: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 37.585, against a charged_total of SGD 37.74. The difference is roughly SGD 0.16, far below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so POL-RD-02 produces NO_ACTION in any event. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries it.

The deviation is established but is nowhere near MATERIAL. The excess of 5.98 km is 24.92% of the 24.0 km optimal: it clears the establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but falls well short of the materiality gate of 50% or 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile inquiry is not triggered at all. For completeness, were it triggered it would find nothing: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588, so no pattern under POL-RD-06 exists. This is an ordinary unavoidable detour, not a material one.

The driver discharges the burden POL-RD-08 places on him by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause, not by a general complaint that traffic was bad. Traffic advisory ADV-20260803-014, a third-party LTA_DATAMALL closure of the very segment the optimal route uses, is invoked under POL-RD-03. That is precisely the discharge the clause demands of the driver once the rider has shown excess.

The chat log shows the diversion was announced in advance and not contested. At 07:54:20 the driver messaged the rider in-app that the PIE towards Tuas was closed by a lorry fire and that he was coming off at Bukit Panjang; the rider read the message at 07:54:48 and replied at 07:54:55 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. The driver's contemporaneous account matches the LTA advisory and the trace, which is why his account of the closure should be preferred over the rider's later recollection.

There is no ERP or toll pass-through correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09. The fare breakdown carries tolls_erp of 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the optimal route crosses no gantry at this hour (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Even on the rider's best case, the standalone pass-through limb of POL-RD-09(2) has nothing to settle and adds nothing to the claim.

The rider's assertion 'I did not see any closure' cites no artifact and is contradicted by a timestamped government advisory covering the disputed segment. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded; it cannot outweigh ADV-20260803-014, which was active from 07:10 and covered the whole trip window. The rider's own profile is context only and she meets none of the gateways that would let any profile field stand in for evidence about this trip.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: you are right that the car went further than it should have. The governing measurement is the trace figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 29.98 km (not the rounded 30.0 km on the trip record), against a booked optimal of 24.0 km. That is an excess of 5.98 km, or 24.9%, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (>0.8 km and >20%), so a deviation is established — your first two points are accepted, and nothing turns on your profile, which does not engage the extra-corroboration rule. But the deviation is fully excused. LTA advisory ADV-20260803-014 closed the PIE towards Tuas between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit from 07:10 to 09:30 that morning — a segment the optimal route (BKE southbound, then PIE westbound) traverses, in the middle of your trip — and the trace shows the car leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed stretch and rejoining by the AYE, exactly the signposted diversion. Under POL-RD-03 that excuses the additional distance up to a cap of 1.30 × (29.2 − 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. Your submission is that the cap must leave something to refund; that is correct as a matter of law, but on these figures the cap is not reached — the whole 5.98 km sits under the 7.76 km ceiling — so there is nothing left to refund. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, and running POL-RD-02 against it (duration 30.0 × 29.98/24.0 = 37.5 min) gives a recomputed fare of SGD 37.585 against the SGD 37.74 charged: a difference of about SGD 0.16, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. Your alternative computation of SGD 31.00 on the booked optimum is rejected because POL-RD-02 must run against the closure-adjusted route where POL-RD-03 excuses the excess. Your recollection that you saw no closure cites no evidence ID and is contradicted by a timestamped government advisory, so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08. There are no ERP or toll lines on this trip (tolls_erp 0.00, no gantries), so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct. To the driver: your account is accepted. The advisory, the trace and the chat log agree — you told the rider at 07:54 that the PIE was closed by a lorry fire and that you were coming off at Bukit Panjang, and the route matches. The deviation is not material (24.9% and 5.98 km are below the 50% / 8.0 km gates), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered and no conduct referral arises; even if it were, deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 588 trips. No escalation trigger applies: the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps), trip identifiers match across all artifacts, and every artifact carries full weight (1.0). The charge stands as billed. Confidence 0.9, resting on the traffic advisory and the GPS trace, both at weight 1.0.
